# Contact Center Reporting: A Complete Guide


October 7, 2026 • 27 MIN READ


Authors


Aishwarya Suresh is an experienced content writer specializing in social media management, social listening, social analytics, Voice of the Customer (VoC) and customer experience. She writes practical, research-backed guides that help brands understand customer conversations, measure social media performance and turn insights into meaningful business decisions.


[View full bio](https://www.sprinklr.com/blog/author/aishwarya-suresh/)


**Key Takeaways:**


- Contact center reporting turns customer conversations, agent activity and operational data into insights that improve service quality, efficiency and business outcomes.
- The most effective reports connect customer experience metrics like CSAT and FCR with operational metrics such as service levels, staffing, and forecast accuracy.
- Modern reporting goes beyond historical dashboards by using AI to uncover contact drivers, detect anomalies, and identify coaching opportunities in real time.
- As self-service and AI agents handle more interactions, reporting must measure automation quality, containment and escalation outcomes alongside human-agent performance.
- Reporting delivers the most value when insights lead directly to action, whether that means improving workflows, coaching agents, optimizing staffing, or fixing customer pain points.


Contact center reporting is how service teams measure what customers are experiencing, how agents are performing, and where operations need attention.


Most leaders already have the numbers. CSAT slipped two points this month. Volume is climbing on Tuesdays. Handle time crept past target last week. What the numbers rarely tell you is which one of those is the cause and which one is just the first symptom to show up on a dashboard.


Reading those signals correctly gets harder as AI takes on more of the queue. Forrester expects one in four brands to see a[10%](https://www.forrester.com/blogs/2026-the-year-ai-gets-real-for-customer-service-but-its-not-glamorous-work/) increase in successful simple self-service interactions by the end of 2026 and also warns that service quality will dip for many organizations as they work through the operational demands of AI deployment. Both can happen inside the same contact center in the same quarter, and your reporting is what tells you which one you are looking at.


That gap is where reporting earns its keep. Good reporting ties a customer signal back to the operational reason behind it, so you know whether to coach a team, fix a workflow, rewrite a knowledge article or hand the finding to the product owner who can actually solve it.


This guide covers the types of contact center reports, the metrics worth tracking, how reporting improves contact center performance, and what reporting needs to look like now that AI handles a growing share of customer conversations.

##


What is contact center reporting?


Contact center reporting is the process of collecting, organizing and presenting data from customer interactions and service operations to measure customer satisfaction, agent performance, and operational efficiency.


Every conversation in a contact center generates data. Voice calls, chats, messages, emails, social conversations, surveys, and AI-assisted interactions all leave behind signals about what customers need and how effectively the organization responds.


Contact center reporting brings these signals together in dashboards, scorecards and reports. This gives agents, supervisors, and customer service leaders a shared view of performance and helps them identify trends, compare results with goals, and make informed decisions.


Modern contact center reporting extends beyond historical performance summaries. AI-powered reporting and analytics can help organizations identify contact drivers, surface conversation trends, detect service bottlenecks, and find opportunities to improve agent coaching, self-service and operational processes.


Contact center reporting commonly includes:


- **Data collection:** Gathering data from various sources within the contact center, such as automatic call distribution, CRM, IVR, workforce management, quality management, and digital customer service platforms.
- **Data processing** : Organizing and formatting raw data into a usable format for analysis.
- **KPI definition** : Defining key performance indicators (KPIs) that align with business goals and[customer service objectives](https://www.sprinklr.com/blog/customer-service-objectives/) .
- **Report creation** : Presenting the most relevant information through dashboards, scorecards, and scheduled reports.
- **Data analysis** : Examining the reports to identify trends, patterns, and areas for improvement in[contact center operations](https://www.sprinklr.com/blog/contact-center-operations/) .
- **Performance evaluation** : Assessing agent performance based on metrics like first-call resolution, AHT, customer satisfaction scores, etc.
- **Forecasting and planning** : Using historical data to predict future call volumes and staffing needs, enabling effective resource allocation.
- **Quality assurance monitoring** : Evaluating the quality of customer interactions through methods like[quality monitoring](https://www.sprinklr.com/blog/quality-monitoring/) , scoring, and feedback.
- **Feedback and coaching** : Providing agents with feedback on their performance and offering coaching or training to address areas for improvement.
- **Compliance tracking** : Ensuring that agents adhere to company policies and regulatory requirements in their interactions.
- **Continuous optimization** : Using insights from reports to implement changes in processes, workflows, and staffing levels to enhance performance.
- **Feedback loop management** : Establishing mechanisms to collect feedback from customers and agents for ongoing process improvement.
- **Custom reporting** : Creating reports for different roles, business units, customer segments, or operational objectives.


** ***Read more:*** **[Contact Center Analytics: KPIs, Capabilities & What Comes Next](https://www.sprinklr.com/blog/contact-center-analytics/) **


***How is contact center reporting different from contact center analytics?***


**Contact center reporting** presents what happened. It organizes interaction and operational data into dashboards, scorecards, and reports so teams can see whether performance met its target. **Contact center analytics** explains why it happened. It examines relationships between data points, identifies root causes, and predicts likely outcomes. Reporting can show that repeat contacts rose 12% last month. Analytics helps identify which contact reason, journey stage, or process change caused it.


##


Types of contact center reports


Automation and AI have made contact center reporting more comprehensive than ever. Contact center reports can be broadly categorized into three types:


1. Agent performance reports


2. Customer satisfaction reports


3. Contact center performance reports


4. AI and self-service reports


Let’s take a look at the most common reports under each category frequently used to assess quality management and[contact center operations](https://www.sprinklr.com/blog/contact-center-operations/) .


### 1. Agent performance reports


#### Agent availability report


The agent availability report highlights agents' login and logout times, total logged-in times, and more. Hence, it accurately reports the number of available and unavailable agents in your contact center at a given time.


#### Agent activity report


Agent activity reports cover key metrics such as average handling time, first-contact resolution and percentage of unanswered calls, typically reflecting agents' activities on a particular day, week, month or quarter. Other key aspects reflected in this report are:


· Number of interactions offered to an agent


· Number of interactions handled by an agent


· Number of unique profiles handled by an agent


· Average interaction duration from connection to disconnection


· Percentage of the number of tickets resolved within the SLA


· Average time taken to resolve/close a ticket


· Top agents by reply time


· Top agents by no. of replies


· Top agents by interactions handled


· Top agents by average handling time (AHT)


**Good to know:** Advanced unified omnichannel platforms allow supervisors to customize[agent performance reports](https://www.sprinklr.com/help/articles/reporting-analytics/agent-performance-report/63ec9d52ef1b447d6c62dd60/) for channels like voice, social, email and live chat.


#### Quality management report


[Quality management](https://www.sprinklr.com/help/articles/what-is-quality-management/quality-management/63fc2f139b334f7283b4e27c/) is a robust reporting instrument, empowering contact centers to excel in customer experiences and elevate agent performance. By scrutinizing customer interactions, whether digital or voice-based, it furnishes quality managers and supervisors with AI-powered agent quality and compliance scores. Conversations can be analyzed and consolidated across channels, forging a singular foundation for contact center metrics.


Newer contact center intelligence capabilities like[Sprinklr’s Contact Center Intelligence](https://www.sprinklr.com/teams/customer-service/contact-center-intelligence/) extend this further. Evaluations can now run across both transcripts and audio, score each agent separately when multiple agents touch a case, and return the reasoning behind a score rather than the score alone.


**Do you know:** Advanced[quality management software](https://www.sprinklr.com/products/customer-service/quality-monitoring/) enables live and virtual agents to switch between channels while keeping the full context of the conversation. Moreover, you can automate your quality assurance with real-time, AI-powered conversational analytics that show you performance, service levels, and CSAT metrics, all without digging for reports.


#### Adherence to schedule


Effectively managing agents' scheduled and actual activities can be a challenging endeavor. Here, the real-time Agent Adherence report provides an all-encompassing solution. This report meticulously compares agents' scheduled activity status with their actual performance and presents this data to supervisors in a user-friendly format. This eliminates the necessity for continuous manual monitoring, ensuring supervisors are kept well informed.


#### Occupancy rate


The occupancy rate report in a contact center provides valuable insights into how efficiently agents are utilized during their working hours. It typically includes agent, availability, idle time, after-call-work time, hold time, meeting and training time, break time, and unavailable time.


#### After-contact work time


After-contact work (ACW) time, also known as wrap-up time, refers to the duration after a customer interaction during which an agent performs tasks related to that interaction. It includes various post-interaction activities to ensure the customer's needs and inquiries are fully addressed and documented.


**Good to know:** Modern[reporting and analytics software](https://www.sprinklr.com/products/customer-service/analytics-and-reporting/) gives supervisors complete visibility into cases handled by their agents and surfaces critical insights such as which channels are used, how customers feel and agent behavior to make decisions on agent self-learning, coaching, scheduling and engagement strategies.


### 2. Customer satisfaction reports


#### Customer feedback report


Agents and supervisors use this report to gauge customer feedback about service quality. This report analyzes three main feedback metrics:


- [Customer satisfaction (CSAT)](https://www.sprinklr.com/blog/customer-satisfaction/) : To gauge the extent to which customers are happy when they interact with your company.
- [Customer effort score (CES)](https://www.sprinklr.com/blog/customer-effort-score/) : Indicates the amount of effort customers usually expend while interacting with your business.
- [Net promoter score (NPS)](https://www.sprinklr.com/blog/net-promoter-score/) : Quantifies customer loyalty by asking customers how likely they are to recommend your company or product, rated on a 0-10 scale.


**Good to know:** Modern customer satisfaction software automates customer surveys across multiple channels, eliminating the redundant work of creating surveys and obtaining customer feedback on a channel-by-channel basis. Moreover, you can trigger and send surveys automatically without relying on agents.


#### Customer retention report


The[customer retention](https://www.sprinklr.com/blog/customer-retention/) rate report provides insights into how effectively a company retains its existing customers over a specified time period. The formula to calculate the retention rate is as follows:


In addition, this report also includes:


· Churned customers


· Reasons for customer churn


· Impact on revenue


***Which contact center reports matter most for executive leadership?***


Executives rarely need queue-level details. They need reports that connect service performance to customer and commercial consequences. That usually means CSAT or customer effort, first contact resolution, repeat contact rate, service level, cost per resolution, top contact drivers and automation resolution quality, each shown as a trend against target rather than a single-period snapshot. The useful addition for most leadership dashboards is repeat contact paired with contact drivers. Together they show how much of this month's volume the business created for itself, which is the number that tends to unlock cross-functional action.


### 3. Contact center performance report


#### Service level agreement (SLA) report


[SLAs](https://www.sprinklr.com/blog/service-level-agreement/) lay down performance benchmarks for contact centers. An SLA report displays the mandatory metrics and your center's performance against each metric. For example, a contact center may set a target of answering a defined percentage of interactions within a defined number of seconds, with different thresholds for voice and digital channels. An SLA report shows the supervisors:


- How many times has an SLA been breached?
- Number of agents and their names who are unable to stick to the SLA guidelines.
- When did the breach happen - during peak or lean hours?


**Good to know:** SLA management has become easier today. You can define, customize, and optimize SLA policies for different support platforms. In addition, set custom escalation policies and send alerts automatically to the suitable supervisor when SLA time approaches.


#### Workforce management report


The[Workforce management (WFM)](https://www.sprinklr.com/blog/workforce-management/) report encompasses forecasting, anomaly detection, staffing, reporting, scheduling, alerts, notifications, and employee leave details. These help supervisors ensure proper resource allocation, forecast staffing needs, monitor schedule adherence, track performance, monitor compliance, and optimize costs.


**Good to know:** From forecasting to capacity planning, omnichannel scheduling and customized reports and alerts, advanced call center[workforce management software](https://www.sprinklr.com/products/customer-service/workforce-management/) helps you accurately predict your workforce needs, improve efficiencies and cut down administrative workload by 30%.


#### IVR performance report


The IVR (Interactive Voice Response) performance report provides an evaluation of how effectively the[IVR system](https://www.sprinklr.com/blog/interactive-voice-responses/) is functioning within a contact center. It includes various key metrics and data points related to the IVR system's performance. Here are the typical components of an IVR Performance Report:


1. **Call completion rate:** This measures the percentage of calls that successfully navigate through the IVR system and reach the intended destination, whether it's self-service options or agent routing.


2. **IVR response time:** This indicates the average time it takes for the IVR system to respond to a caller's input or request. Shorter response times generally lead to a smoother customer experience.


3. **Menu navigation success rate:** It evaluates the percentage of callers who successfully navigate the IVR menu options to reach their desired destination without encountering issues or missteps.


4. **Abandonment rate within IVR:** This tracks the percentage of callers who hang up or abandon the call while interacting with the IVR system. A high abandonment rate within the IVR may indicate usability issues.


5. **Call deflection:** This measures the percentage of calls that are resolved within the IVR system without the need for agent intervention, indicating the effectiveness of self-service options.


6. **Error handling:** It assesses how well the IVR system handles errors or misunderstandings in caller input, ensuring that callers can recover and continue their interaction smoothly.


7. **IVR Survey Results:** If post-interaction surveys are incorporated into the IVR system, this provides feedback on the caller's experience and satisfaction with the IVR process.


8. **IVR load and performance testing results:** This includes data on how the IVR system handles peak call volumes and whether any performance issues arise under high load.


9. **IVR outage or downtime information:** Records any instances of IVR system downtime, which may impact overall call handling efficiency.


### 4. AI and self-service reports


This category did not exist in most contact center reporting stacks a few years ago. It does now, because a growing share of interactions never reaches a human agent.


An AI and self-service report typically tracks:


· **Self-service resolution rate:** Eligible interactions resolved without human assistance and without a qualifying repeat contact.


· **Containment rate:** Interactions that stayed within the automated journey.


· **Fallback rate:** How often the system failed to interpret intent and moved the customer to a default path.


· **Escalation and handoff quality:** Whether context, history and customer intent carried over to the agent.


· **Intent recognition and response accuracy:** How reliably the system understood and answered correctly.


· **Repeat contact after automation:** Customers who came back through another channel after an automated interaction.


· **Customer effort and satisfaction post-automation:** Whether the experience was genuinely easier.


Read containment alongside resolution and repeat contact. A customer who stayed inside an automated journey because they could not find a way to reach an agent still counts as contained, which is why containment on its own tends to flatter the numbers.


***How should contact centers measure AI agent performance?***


Measure AI agents on the same customer outcomes you use for human agents, then add the operational metrics unique to automation. The shared outcomes are resolution, customer satisfaction, customer effort, repeat contact, and compliance. The automation-specific measures are containment, fallback rate, escalation rate, handoff quality, intent recognition accuracy, response latency, and cost per automated resolution. Break these down by contact reason rather than reviewing them in aggregate. Automation usually performs well on a narrow set of simple, high-volume intents and poorly on complex or emotionally charged ones, and an average across both hides exactly the intents you need to pull back from automation.


##


How reporting enhances your contact center performance


Contact center reporting provides accurate and timely information on:


· Progress of daily tasks


· The efficiency of agents and processes


· The state and impact of[customer service](https://www.sprinklr.com/blog/what-is-customer-service/)


Here are other ways contact center reporting impacts the output:


- **Strategic decision making:** Contact center performance reports are invaluable for you to make informed, data-driven decisions. By meticulously analyzing these reports, latent trends and patterns within your workforce and processes are highlighted. This insightful data empowers you to implement targeted changes in hiring strategies, refine training programs, adopt advanced technologies, and fine-tune overall contact center management. For instance, if reports reveal a surge in call volumes during specific hours, you can strategically adjust staffing levels to ensure adequate coverage.
- **Shapes the customer experience:** Utilizing insights from customer satisfaction reports can be transformative for your contact center. Implementing the recommendations derived from these reports can significantly enhance mission-critical customer support metrics, such as customer satisfaction (CSAT) and customer retention. By understanding what resonates with your customers, the contact center can refine strategies and practices, ensuring a consistently exceptional experience that fosters loyalty and trust.
- **Evaluates agent performance:** Contact center reporting maps agent-customer interactions, assesses agent performance against set goals and ensures adherence to organizational guidelines. It aids in identifying performance gaps and agents in need of additional training.
- **Leads to cost optimization:** Monitoring every aspect of your contact center can be both challenging and costly. Reporting highlights areas that require streamlining. For instance, implementing[skill-based routing](https://www.sprinklr.com/blog/skill-based-routing/) for quicker call resolution can lead to time and cost savings.
- **Improves operational efficiency:** By dissecting key performance metrics, you can pinpoint areas that require optimization. This data-driven approach allows for strategic resource allocation, streamlined workflows, and the implementation of technology solutions, resulting in a more agile and cost-effective operation.
- **Compliance and regulations:** Contact center reporting meticulously monitors and enhances agent compliance with scripts, policies and regulatory requirements. It significantly mitigates the risk of compliance issues, fortifying the contact center's ability to operate within legal and industry-mandated parameters. This not only safeguards the business but also fosters trust with customers who rely on secure and compliant interactions.

##


11 key metrics and KPIs in contact center reporting


Contact center reporting has evolved over the years, with customer experience and agent performance proving to be the critical indicators of contact center success. The following metrics surrounding both are observed across all contact centers.:


### 1. Quality assurance score


The Quality Assurance (QA) Score is a critical metric that evaluates the quality of interactions between agents and customers. It involves a systematic assessment of calls or interactions based on predefined criteria, such as adherence to scripts, empathy, active listening and resolution accuracy. The QA score provides a quantitative measure of how well agents are meeting established quality standards.


A high QA score signifies that agents consistently deliver high-quality service, ensuring customer satisfaction and loyalty. On the other hand, a low QA score may indicate areas for improvement in agent training, coaching, or process refinement.


***Related Read:***[Top 13 Call Center Quality Assurance Best Practices](https://www.sprinklr.com/blog/call-center-quality-assurance-best-practices/)


### 2. First response time (FRT)


[First response time](https://www.sprinklr.com/customer-service-glossary/first-response-time/) measures how long a customer waits for the first agent reply after reaching out. On messaging, email and social, this is the main responsiveness metric. For voice, average speed of answer does the same job.


**Interpretation:** The lower the response times, the better.


*Read Story on how*[Uber](https://www.sprinklr.com/stories/uber/) *used Sprinklr to enhance customer service: with 33% reduction in FRT and increased SLA compliance; while supporting the company's global growth.*


### 3. First contact resolution (FCR)


[First contact resolution](https://www.sprinklr.com/blog/first-contact-resolution/) is the percentage of customer queries an agent resolves and closes the query in the first contact without transferring, pausing or escalating it. A high FCR percentage indicates efficient and satisfactory customer service, as it minimizes customer effort and frustration.


**Interpretation:** The higher the first contact resolution, the better. Define your repeat-contact window and exclusions up front, since FCR shifts considerably depending on whether a follow-up two days later on another channel counts against it.


### 4. Abandonment rate


[Abandonment rate](https://www.sprinklr.com/customer-service-glossary/abandonment-rate/) indicates the number of customers who drop off before reaching an agent. The reasons behind a high average call abandonment rate are:


· Longer hold times.


· Overly complex IVR menus.


· Insufficient staffing.


· Ineffective routing systems.


**Interpretation:** The lesser the call abandonment rate, the better. State whether short abandons are included or excluded, since practices vary.


### 5. Average speed of answer


[Average speed of answer](https://www.sprinklr.com/customer-service-glossary/average-speed-of-answer/) measures the average time it takes for calls to be answered by agents once they enter the queue. It provides valuable insights into the responsiveness of the contact center.


**Interpretation:** A low ASA indicates that calls are being handled promptly, contributing to positive customer experiences. Conversely, a high ASA suggests longer wait times, which can lead to customer frustration and dissatisfaction.


ASA applies to voice queues. For messaging, email, and social, use first response time instead, since those channels measure responsiveness differently.


By monitoring and managing ASA, contact centers can fine-tune their staffing levels, optimize call routing strategies, and implement[interactive voice response (IVR)](https://www.sprinklr.com/blog/interactive-voice-responses/) systems to improve responsiveness and reduce wait times.


### 6. Average handle time (AHT)


[Average handle time](https://www.sprinklr.com/blog/average-handle-time/) is a metric used in contact centers to measure the average duration of a customer call interaction from when a customer initiates a phone call to the time of final resolution. The duration includes talk time, hold time, transfers, and any after-call work (ACW) that an agent must perform post-interaction to resolve the customer query.


**Interpretation:** A lower AHT often indicates efficient and streamlined customer service. However, it's essential to balance AHT with other factors like quality of service to ensure that speed doesn't compromise the effectiveness of customer interactions. Note that digital channels need their own definition, since agents handle concurrent conversations and asynchronous replies.


### 7. Agent adherence to process


Agent adherence to process assesses how well agents follow prescribed conversation guidelines during customer interactions. This metric is crucial for maintaining consistency and ensuring that agents convey accurate and on-brand information to customers.


**Interpretation:** High adherence indicates that agents are effectively using provided resources to deliver standardized, reliable information. However, it's essential to balance adherence with the ability to adapt to unique customer needs.


Monitoring adherence allows contact centers to identify areas for improvement in training and guidance effectiveness. It also helps maintain compliance with regulatory requirements and internal policies.


### 8. Service level


Service level measures the efficiency of a contact center in terms of responsiveness. It represents the percentage of interactions answered within a specified timeframe, typically expressed as a service level goal (e.g., 80% of calls answered within 20 seconds).


Maintaining a high service level is crucial for delivering prompt and satisfactory customer service. Regular monitoring of service level metrics allows contact centers to proactively manage call volume, staffing, and resource allocation to meet or exceed customer expectations for responsiveness consistently.


***Here’s***[How to Measure Call Center Service Level](https://www.sprinklr.com/blog/call-center-service-level/)


### 9. Forecast accuracy


Forecast accuracy is a vital metric that evaluates the precision of predicted call volumes and other contact center metrics compared to actual results. It measures how well the contact center's forecasting models align with real-world operational data.


There is no single formula used consistently across contact centers. Teams commonly use absolute percentage error or weighted absolute percentage error, so your report should state which method it applies and show forecast bias separately.


Accurate forecasting is essential for effective resource planning, ensuring that the right number of agents are available to handle expected call volumes. A high forecast accuracy indicates that your contact center can reliably anticipate customer demand and allocate resources accordingly.


However, if there are significant disparities between forecasts and actual volumes, it may lead to issues like understaffing or overstaffing, which can negatively impact your service levels and operational costs.


### 10. Customer satisfaction score (CSAT)


Measuring how happy your customers are with your service is a simple metric. You can calculate customer satisfaction by asking customers to rate your service on a scale of 1 to 5 or 1 to 10. The percentage of customers who score you between 8 and 10, or 4 and 5, make up your[CSAT](https://www.sprinklr.com/help/articles/customer-satisfaction-analysis/what-is-csat-and-how-is-it-scored/65a8f025d39ae90f84200c38/) score.


**Interpretation** : A high CSAT score indicates that customers are content with the service they receive. Report response rate alongside the score, since a low or uneven response rate limits how far the result can be generalized.


### 11. Customer effort score (CES)


The[customer effort score](https://www.sprinklr.com/blog/customer-effort-score/) measures how much effort your customers have to expend to resolve their queries.


CES is calculated differently depending on the survey design. A common approach asks customers how strongly they agree with a statement such as " *The company made it easy for me to resolve my issue.* " Responses are collected on a defined scale, and the score is reported as an average or as the percentage of customers selecting the easier end of the scale.


**Interpretation** : The higher, the better. A low CES indicates that customers found the process difficult and may be at risk for dissatisfaction and attrition. When the question is positively worded, a higher score means less customer effort. Because methodologies vary, document the exact question, scale and calculation on the report, so results stay comparable over time.


Interested to learn more? Check out the full list of[contact center metrics](https://www.sprinklr.com/blog/contact-center-metrics/) here.


***Why do two contact center dashboards show different numbers for the same metric?***


Because they are almost never measuring the same thing. The usual culprits are differing formulas, time zones, refresh schedules, channel scopes and filters, along with inconsistent treatment of transfers, short abandons, reopened cases and interactions that span more than one channel. Two teams can each be technically correct and still report a different FCR for the same week. The fix is a metric dictionary that records the formula, data source, included and excluded interactions, filters, time zone, refresh cadence, and a named owner for every KPI.

##


Steps to improve contact center performance by efficient reporting


By following the below steps, you can harness the power of efficient reporting to drive tangible improvements in your contact center's performance and overall customer satisfaction levels.


### 1. Define clear objectives


Before delving into reporting, it's imperative to establish clear and specific objectives for your contact center. These objectives should align with your overall business goals and customer service strategy. Are you aiming to enhance customer satisfaction, increase first-call resolution rates, or optimize agent productivity? This clarity not only enables you to focus on collecting and analyzing data but also serves as a benchmark for measuring the effectiveness of your reporting initiatives.


### 2. Select relevant metrics


Two primary factors should guide your metric selection process: alignment with organizational goals and impact on the Customer Experience (CX).


· **Alignment with organizational goals:** Each metric you choose should directly contribute to attaining your business objectives. For example, if your overarching goal is to increase customer loyalty, metrics related to customer satisfaction scores and Net Promoter Scores (NPS) become crucial indicators.


· **Impact on CX:** Consider how each metric influences the customer's experience. Metrics that directly impact CX should be prioritized. For instance, first-call resolution and average handling time directly affect how customers perceive the efficiency and effectiveness of your service.


### 3. Define each metric before you report it


Record the formula, data source, included and excluded interactions, filters, time zone, refresh cadence and owner for every KPI. This single step prevents most cross-team disputes about whose dashboard is correct, and it becomes essential once AI-handled and human-handled interactions sit in the same report.


### 4. Implement advanced reporting tools


Utilize robust reporting software or tools to process and present data in a comprehensible and actionable format. Ensure these tools can generate both real-time and historical reports. In addition, it should be able to deliver persona-specific views and reports. Agent reports vary vastly from supervisor reports since their KPIs and focus areas differ. Likewise, it should allow custom as well as curated reports that are easily exportable in varied formats.


### 5. Automate data collection


Streamline data collection from various contact center systems, such as[automatic call dstribution](https://www.sprinklr.com/blog/automatic-call-distribution/) , CRM, IVR, and workforce management. Automation reduces manual efforts and minimizes errors. It does not remove the need to validate data, so keep checking for missing records, duplicates, timestamp mismatches, and broken bot-to-agent handoffs.


### 6. Segment data for deeper insights


Break down data by criteria such as agent, team, time of day, channel, contact reason, customer segment and whether the interaction was handled by a human or automated. This granular approach helps pinpoint specific areas needing attention. An acceptable overall resolution rate can still hide one contact reason or self-service journey that is failing badly.


### 7. Implement real-time monitoring


Integrate real-time reporting capabilities to[manage escalation](https://www.sprinklr.com/blog/escalation-management/) promptly and efficiently. This ensures that corrective actions can be taken immediately to prevent further escalations. Set thresholds carefully and give each alert a named response owner, otherwise volume of alerts becomes its own problem.


### 8. Benchmark against industry standards


Compare your contact center's performance against industry benchmarks or best practices. This provides context and helps set realistic performance targets. Benchmarks vary considerably by sector, so use one relevant to your industry rather than a universal figure.


### 9. Implement agent training and coaching


Use reporting insights to identify areas where agents may need additional training or coaching. Provide targeted support to enhance their skills and knowledge. Share relevant reports with agents to foster a culture of accountability. Encourage them to take ownership of their performance and seek continuous improvement.


### 10. Leverage feedback loops


Use reporting to establish feedback loops with agents and customers. This helps gather valuable insights for process improvement and product/service enhancements.


### 11. Regularly review and adjust strategies


Continuously assess the effectiveness of your strategies based on reporting feedback. Adjust your approach as needed to address evolving customer needs and business goals, and revisit your metric definitions whenever you add channels, automation or new service commitments.
